newsitem.title: FRANCE: Peugeot sees sales rise in Iran.
newsitem.headline: Peugeot sees sales rise in Iran.

text.p: French carmaker Peugeot Automobiles expects to more than double its car sales in Iran this year to around 20,000, a senior company official said on Wednesday.

"We expect to recover the volumes we had in our best days," Peugeot international affairs director Hubert Lehucher told a news conference. He said the group was forecasting 20,000 registrations for 1997.

Peugeot Automobiles, a division of PSA Peugeot Citroen, last year delivered 8,000 kits to assemble 405 models to its partner Iran Khodro after a settlement of Iranian arrears cleared the way for the resumption of state insurance for exports to Iran.
Yves Barbe, deputy managing director of Peugeot Automobiles, said Iran Khodro was investing with the aim of creating production capacity of 200,000 vehicles annually in the next two years.
Barbe said Iran seemed to be "in a rather satisfying economic phase."
Automobiles Peugeot began sending kits for assembly to Iran in 1989.
